prompt: The point $(1, 1)$ sits on $y = x^2$. The graph is stretched to $y = 4x^2$. On the new graph, what is the $y$-value when $x = 1$?
hint: A number multiplying the whole function changes heights only. What happens to each $y$-value when it is multiplied by $4$?

hints.text: A number multiplying the whole function changes heights only. What happens to each $y$-value when it is multiplied by $4$?
Use the new rule at $x = 1$: first find $1^2$, then multiply that result by $4$.
Since $1^2 = 1$ and $4 \times 1 = 4$, the new $y$-value at $x = 1$ is $4$.

explanation: In $a \cdot f(x)$, every $y$-value is multiplied by $a$ while the $x$-values stay the same.
Here $a = 4$, so each point on $y = x^2$ becomes $4$ times as high.
The old height at $x = 1$ was $1$, so the new height is $4 \times 1 = 4$ and the point is $(1, 4)$.

alternativeExplanations.title: A table of heights
steps: Every height is exactly 4 times taller — the sticker got stretched, not slid.
